subject: Renewal + Capacity Increase — KiteCart hosted commit & rate-tier options
messages:
From: Aisha Rana <aisha@kitecart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Philips <tom.philips@kitecart.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window — exploring higher commit + rate caps

Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. KiteCart is headed into our Q4 planning and we expect a ~2.5x increase in conversational traffic (peak shopper experiences + new returns flow).

We're working through the renewal, and would like to discuss:
- Moving from our current 500M/month hosted commit to a 1.2B/month band for 12 months
- Smoother burst handling (we see 3x hourly spikes during campaigns)
- A revised rate-tier for tokens above commit (we currently hit overage twice/month)

Can you send an ops-friendly proposal with the rate tiers, any SLA/latency guardrails for the higher band, and what the onboarding schedule looks like? I can pull procurement in once we have a sketch.

Attachments: KiteCart_MAAP_v2.xlsx (mutual action plan draft)

Thanks,
Aisha
Head of Product
KiteCart

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rana <aisha@kitecart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — exploring higher commit + rate caps

Aisha — appreciate the context and the MAP. High-level response below; attaching a short rate card and a suggested migration timeline. Kimberly and Priya are looped to confirm SLA and legal checkpoints.

Short answers:
- We can support a 1.2B/month committed band.
- For campaign spikes we recommend a 2-stage burst buffer: a soft burst (instant, up to 3x sustained for 2 hours) and a paid emergency burst (higher rate, guaranteed within quota).
- Rate tiers: committing to 1.2B lowers your overage rate by ~28% vs current plan; see attached proposed-ratecard-2026.pdf.

Ops items we'll include in the MAP:
1) Canary rollout window (2 weeks) to pre-warm KV cache and batching profiles
2) Autoscaling policy: target p95 latency under 350ms; soft throttle threshold at 85% of reserved capacity
3) Billing cadence: monthly invoicing with a provisional proration for the first month of uplift

I'll put together a formal proposal and updated MAP by Monday EOD. Any must-have compliance items I should call out?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-ratecard-2026.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: KiteCart renewal — ask for SLA guardrail wording & legal pointers

Kimberly/Priya — quick internal note before I send a formal proposal to KiteCart. They want 1.2B/month commit for 12 months, plus better handling for campaign spikes. Key items for us to confirm: 
- SLA: can we commit to a p95 latency target of 350ms for their default model (r11g-opti) on Dedicated slices during peak, and what fallback language should we include if a region is constrained?
- Burst: propose soft burst up to 3x for 2 hours with automatic admission; emergency burst subject to availability with a pre-defined surcharge. Legal, can we pre-approve the surcharge bands or do you want that redlined per-account?
- Onboarding ops: need a 2-week prewarm/canary with a staging key and access to their biggest prompt sets for cache warmup.

I drafted a short MAP (attached to the outbound). If you can send back suggested SLA snippet and billing wording by EOD Monday I’ll finalize.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Aisha Rana <aisha@kitecart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Philips <tom.philips@kitecart.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — exploring higher commit + rate caps

Thanks Jordan — this looks promising. A few clarifications from our side before procurement: 
- Latency: p95 350ms is fine if it's for the committed pool. If fallbacks can move us to a cheaper model variant during contention, we need explicit notice + automated throttling rules so feature teams aren't surprised.
- Burst: the soft-burst is critical; we need a throttling policy that prefers graceful degradation of non-critical conversation flows (e.g., low-priority async tasks) before dropping core checkout experiences.
- Billing: procurement will want a guaranteed proration and clear invoice line items for "soft burst" vs "emergency burst" usage.

We can share a sample prompt set (anonymized) and a weekly batch of logs for first 30 days to help warm cache. Procurement contact is: kate.su@kitecart.com — you can loop her once the MAP is formalized.

Best,
Aisha

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rana <aisha@kitecart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kate Su <kate.su@kitecart.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — exploring higher commit + rate caps

Aisha/Kate — thanks — attaching the updated MAP with SLA snippet, burst policy language, and an invoice example that separates commit, soft-burst, and emergency-burst lines. Highlights: 
- SLA snippet: p95 latency guarantee for committed capacity; explicit region-fallback clause with 72h notice for planned migrations
- Burst policy: soft-burst auto-admission up to 3x for up to 2 hours; soft-burst billed at the committed token rate (no surcharge). Emergency burst: subject to availability and billed at a premium rate (outlined in the rate card).
- Billing: first-month proration, then month-to-month invoicing; procurement can request monthly usage statements and token-level breakdowns.

Next steps:
1) Kate to confirm procurement line items and PO cadence
2) KiteCart to send anonymized prompt set and first-week logs for prewarm
3) Redwood to provision staging keys and schedule a 2-week canary starting as early as Oct 4

I'll open a HubSpot deal update and share the MAP link.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: KiteCart_MAAP_v2_FINAL.docx, proposed-ratecard-2026.pdf, invoice-example.csv
